2. Task and a physically meaningful boundary
============================================
Task: deliver an unknown qubit through an unavoidable interaction in a forward
physical link or device. The qubit may be entangled with an untouched reference.
The output must retain useful quantum coherence. A perfect local buffer does
not accomplish this forward task. Deliberately introducing a removable noisy
interaction into protected local storage would be a dominated benchmark.

D denotes the current logical input, A a readable and locally addressable
quantum boundary mode, and M every other persistent physical degree of freedom.
During a declared raw/readout/control window, the effective operation acts on
D+A. M does not interact with A or D during this window. Between windows A and
M may undergo arbitrary quantum channels, retain old correlations and respond
to past information. Deployment need not reset, discard or depolarize A.
Past logical outputs and untouched references are isolated from later device
operations. Future logical input wires remain outside the intervening
memory-only dynamics until their declared calls. No bound on dim(M) is used
in the operator theorems.

This is stronger than saying that all coupling is spatially routed through A.
If M can swap a state into A DURING the call, A-only calibration is insufficient.
The isolation window must include the interval after calibration preparation
and before the raw interaction. A hidden bypass cannot be excluded by a finite
set of successful tests. The operation chooses a finite coherent boundary; it
is an actively specified physical architecture, not an inferred property of
an arbitrary uncontrolled system.

Available operations inherited from the programme are full local weak QND
X,Y,Z instruments, Pauli pulses and feedback, local routing/latching, private
matched data Pauli frames and their retirement. The native CNOT port is an
actual selectable interaction when the constructed phase primitive is used.
Trusted full instruments are premises, not merely fitted outcome contrasts.
Errors in an unknown fixed raw map are acquired; errors in trusted references,
leakage of settings, or unmodeled ongoing coupling require their own allowances.

Calibration also needs access to A BEFORE its raw interaction. When A is a
recycled, locally addressable mode, its between-use interval supplies that
port. An outgoing-only environment meter does not supply upstream access.
Six finite weak preparations implement
  rho_AM -> sigma_(i,a) tensor Tr_A rho_AM,
  sigma_(i,a)=(I+a alpha sigma_i)/2,
  i in {X,Y,Z}, a in {+1,-1}, alpha=1-2t_(L_p)>0.
Here t_L is the exact odd-L binomial weak-majority tail. Feedback and private
axial dephasing, with preparation records/keys retired, produce the exact
mixed replacement. No pure source is assumed. The executed generator also
charges actual local Pauli mixing to I/2 before the weak preparation.
Calibration therefore resets A; the later service does not. M continues.

3. The finite operator representation
=====================================
For one fixed physical setting b, expand each raw D+A Kraus operator as
  K_l = sum_s s_D tensor A_(s,l),  s in {I,X,Y,Z}.
Actual matched Pauli frames on D, with their keys retired, remove cross terms:
  T_b = sum_s Ad_s tensor M_(s,b),
  M_(s,b)(X)=sum_l A_(s,l) X A_(s,l)^*.
This is an identity on correlated D/A/M/reference inputs. It is not obtained
by asserting that the unknown apparatus has a classical hidden state.

Define positive input-port effects
  F_(s,b)=M_(s,b)^*(I) >=0,  sum_s F_(s,b)=I_A.
For input port marginal rho_A, the virtual Pauli branch has probability
Tr(F_(s,b)rho_A). The virtual branch is a mathematical positive decomposition;
the observer is not supplied the current microscopic error label.

For a qubit A, each effect has four real coefficients:
  F_(s,b)=f_(s,b,0) I+v_(s,b) dot sigma.
There are16 coefficients per physical setting, independent of dim(M), the
age of the acquired record, or the detailed physical state of M. This is a
task response description. It does not predict arbitrary new controls, the
fine joint meter record, or the subsequent state of M.

For a port of Hilbert-space dimension d_A the analogous count is4 d_A^2 per
setting. A port containing b qubits has exponential4^b cost in general; the
construction does not prove that large interacting systems have a small port.
Known mixed product preparations also have their own conditioning costs as b
grows. Bounded physical access, task structure and acquisition conditioning
remain independent requirements.

4. Exact renewal and the weaker acquired fault envelope
=======================================================
EXACT CENTRAL EFFECTS. Suppose every actual Pauli effect is scalar,
  F_(s,b)=p_(s,b) I_A.
Then M_s/p_s is trace preserving for p_s>0. It may radically alter the memory
and retain information. Nevertheless each specified error string has positive
memory-map effect
  F_(s_1,...,s_K) = (product_j p_(s_j,b_j)) I.
This follows by backward induction: intervening memory-only CPTP adjoints
preserve I, and each error-branch adjoint maps I to p_s I.

After tracing memory at the FINAL boundary, the logical outputs have exactly
the corresponding product Pauli channel, including inputs entangled across
uses or initially correlated with memory. A is allowed to be recycled. No
vacuum event, finite memory dimension, entropy bound, or forgetting rate is
needed. A fixed setting or an exogenous fixed schedule is sufficient. Fine
record conditioning or record-dependent settings do not inherit one fixed
product law. The logical service averages the retired frame keys and declared
meter/control records. Its full fine-record instrument remains distinct.

APPROXIMATE CENTRALITY. If a valid Pauli probability vector p obeys
  delta=(1/2) sum_s ||F_s-p_s I||_infinity,
then the current output, after tracing the local port, is within delta in
half diamond norm of Pauli(p) composed with that trace. The proof uses the
identity that the completely bounded norm of a partial-trace effect map for
Hermitian H is ||H||. The same finite stream of isolated logical outputs has
allowance at most K delta: replace the final task by the independent Pauli
channel, then proceed backwards. Once later logical tasks are independent,
their intervening memory-only channels can be traced out. The uniform current
bound applies with all earlier/future logical wires as references at each
hybrid step. This is a finite-horizon allowance, not exact independence forever.

ACQUIRED BAD-EFFECT BOUND. A more durable certificate is
  F_bad=sum_(s!=I)F_s = I-F_I <= q I_A.                 (1)
For any normalized conditional physical state, the virtual bad-branch chance
is at most q. For any specified set S of faulty uses, backward positivity gives
  Pr(all uses in S are bad) <= q^|S|.                  (2)
Unspecified uses are summed as their actual trace-preserving operations.
The theorem allows quantum correlations and history-dependent memory dynamics.
It also follows that the total virtual fault count is stochastically dominated
by Binomial(K,q); the causal conditional fault probability is bounded after
any past positive branch. This is an unconditional statement, not one obtained
by conditioning on future acceptance. It cannot simply be transplanted to the
previous secret-slot globally postselected packets.

For a current task, (1) bounds the half-diamond distance to an ideal logical
identity with the SAME total environment channel by q. Replace each bad Pauli
by I while leaving its positive memory map unchanged; both bad contributions
have norm at most q. For a fresh Bell input initially independent of the
apparatus, with untouched reference, fidelity is at least1-q for every port
state. A bound q<1/2 therefore certifies entanglement
survival. This is not a quantum-capacity or fault-tolerance threshold theorem.

Centrality of F_I alone makes the total bad indicator state independent; it
does not make all individual Pauli types independent. In particular the finite
constructed phase primitive adds small X/Y faults, whose individual effects
need not be central even when F_I is flattened. The executed acquisition
claims (1), not exact iid noise.

FOCUSED REVIEW OF ACQUIRED_BOUNDARY_EFFECTS_AND_TASK_RENEWAL.txt
25 October2026

Reviewed the actual integrated source, especially Sections3-4 and the physical
boundary in Section2. No incorrect algebra or quantitative bound was found in
the reviewed central-effect, acquired bad-effect or approximate-centrality
statements under their declared fixed closed-port assumptions.

1. Arbitrary initial correlations
The Pauli expansion/twirl is a joint-channel identity on D+A with M and an
external reference carried along. It therefore applies to correlated inputs.
The virtual error probability depends on the A marginal through Tr(F_s rho_A).
It does not require a product input. Exact central effects imply that each
composed error-string memory map has scalar effect, so tracing memory only
at the end gives the product logical channel on the initial logical marginal.

2. K delta approximate centrality
The stated backward hybrid is valid. Replace the last task together with the
final ancillary trace; its error is bounded with every other logical wire as
a reference. Once that task is an independent Pauli map, the preceding
memory-only channel can be erased under the final trace. Repeat backwards.
This yields sum_j delta_j, hence K delta in the uniform case. It does not
require inventing an ideal continuing-memory state after an intermediate
approximate replacement.

Necessary scope clarification: all other logical registers, including future
input wires in the multi-use channel formulation, must remain outside the
intervening memory-only dynamics until their declared task use. The source's
isolated-output and untouched-reference assumptions convey the intended model;
an explicit sentence about future logical wires avoids ambiguity. Fine-record
dependent control does not inherit a fixed product law unless separately
covered by an appropriate channel/control comparison.

3. q fault bounds
F_bad<=qI gives conditional virtual bad probability<=q after every earlier
positive branch. Specified fault-set bounds q^|S| and binomial domination follow.
No iid microscopic model is required. Every deployed actual menu must obey
the same bound, and the private-mixture causal ordering must hold. Future
postselection or control that leaks the arm before A is fixed is outside the
claim. The same-environment-channel half-diamond comparison<=q also follows:
the actual and Pauli-replaced bad CP maps both have norm at most q.

4. Bell witness
For an exactly maximally entangled D-reference input, that pure input is
necessarily initially independent of the apparatus. Explicitly stating this
independence is preferable. Then the intended Bell weight is at least1-q for
every A/M state, so q<1/2 certifies entanglement. The arbitrary-correlations
channel theorem is broader, but it should not be used to describe an arbitrary
already-correlated input as a fresh Bell resource.

5. Meaningful unassisted model control
For the executed raw V=(4+3i)(6X+2Y+3Z)/35, Tr(V)=0. With A marginal I/2 and
logical input independent of the apparatus, discarding/ignoring A gives
off-diagonal multiplier Tr(V rho_A)=0 (or its complex conjugate, according
to the chosen matrix block). Hence the raw logical channel is complete Z
dephasing. Applied to half of a Bell pair it produces
  (|00><00|+|11><11|)/2,
with Bell fidelity1/2 and separable output. The acquired final service bound
q<13/40 guarantees Bell fidelity>27/40 for this same input-probe state and
indeed for every allowed probe state. This is a useful model-controlled task
contrast, not evidence that the received observer was given V, or a general
quantum-capacity advantage. An unprovided echo/uncomputation port must not be
smuggled into either side of the stated boundary.

No broad numerical tests were added for this focused review. It relies on the
integrated derivation and the already executed independent841-case checks.
